name: Pollen-Shard
description: Pollen-Shard is a tiny, airless rock tumbling through space in an eccentric orbit that brings it alternately close to its star and far into the cold beyond. Its surface is a museum of impacts, every square kilometer cratered and re-cratered until the original terrain is impossible to reconstruct. Fine regolith dust, electrostatically charged by constant solar wind bombardment, drifts across the surface in slow-motion waves that give the world its name, resembling golden pollen scattered on dark stone.

Without atmosphere, Pollen-Shard exists in absolute silence. The only sensations are the crunch of regolith underfoot transmitted through suit boots and the visual spectacle of the electrostatically levitating dust, which floats in gossamer sheets above the surface at the terminator line where day meets night. Temperature extremes are savage, the sunlit side hot enough to soften exposed metals while the dark side drops to temperatures that liquefy common gases. The transition between the two can occur over mere meters.

An escape pod debris field on Pollen-Shard's equatorial ridge tells a story no one has yet fully pieced together. The pods are from a vessel of unknown registry, their design incorporating elements from multiple manufacturing traditions, and they appear to have been deliberately aimed at this specific location rather than ejected in emergency. Whatever the pods carried was removed before any survey team arrived, leaving only the shells and fragments of a manifest in a language that resists translation.

Pollen-Shard's iron and silicon deposits are unremarkable, but the escape pod mystery draws occasional investigators. The pods' trajectory analysis suggests they originated from a direction with no charted systems, and the materials in their construction include alloys not in any standard database. Someone, or something, chose this insignificant rock as a drop point, and the careful removal of the pods' contents suggests they will return. The dust continues its patient drift across the evidence, slowly burying what remains.
